title: Window capture keeps the shadow and rounded corners
goal: When you capture a window by clicking it, the result should look like the window itself: its drop shadow around it and see-through rounded corners, the way the built-in macOS window capture does, instead of a hard rectangle with the desktop showing through the corners.
notes: Today the click path crops the frozen full-screen bitmap to the window bounds (RectSelectionController.finish -> crop). The system look needs a per-window capture (SCScreenshotManager with an SCContentFilter for that window id, or CGWindowListCreateImage with kCGWindowImageBoundsIgnoreFraming off) taken at freeze time or after dismiss; note the filter path drops shadows unless asked for them. Depends on next-window-capture.
acceptance: Clicking a window during a region capture produces an image with the window shadow and transparent rounded corners, matching the system window capture
A setting or modifier lets you capture the bare bounds instead, and the audit says which is the default
